Subject: Clarify what Redwood keeps by default (requests / responses / prompts / outputs)

Hi Kimberly,

Quick question from our security team as we prepare for procurement: can you confirm what Redwood retains by default for hosted API customers? Specifically we need clarity on:

- Are raw customer requests (the full prompt) stored by default?
- Are model outputs (responses) retained, and for how long?
- When a session is streamed, do intermediate tokens get persisted anywhere?
- If customers upload attachments to be processed, are the attachments stored and for how long?
- What is the process for a customer-initiated erasure request and what evidence do you provide that deletion completed?

We’re trying to decide whether Hosted API meets our compliance needs or whether we need to request a Dedicated/Private deployment. If you can point us to a short summary or timeline that we can drop into our security questionnaire, that would be ideal.

Thanks,
Elena Ruiz
Head of Security - HealthCo

Hi Elena — thanks for the clear list. Summary below is for Redwood hosted API (default settings). I’ve attached a short PDF that you can include in your questionnaire.

High-level defaults (hosted API):
- User requests (full prompt text): retained by default for 45 days for debugging, quality monitoring, and fraud detection.
- Model outputs (final responses): retained by default for 45 days and then removed unless flagged for debugging or legal hold.
- Streamed/intermediate tokens: treated as ephemeral; buffer is kept only in-memory for request processing and not persisted to our long-term store by default. Any persisted stream fragments would be an opt-in diagnostic path or customer request.
- Attachments uploaded for processing: retained for up to 90 days by default to allow retries and exports; shorter retention can be configured per customer.

Erasure process (customer-initiated):
- Request received via support portal or API: start the erasure workflow.
- Automated purge: best-effort automatic deletion of default-retained artifacts within 7 business days.
- Evidence: we can provide audit logs showing deletion events (object IDs and timestamps). For Hosted customers we typically provide a deletion confirmation package (log excerpts + signed statement).

Options for stricter controls:
- Dedicated tenancy: shorter retention, configurable purge windows, and access to detailed deletion evidence tied to reserved capacity.
- Private / on-prem: customer-managed storage; Redwood provides the runbook for purge but does not host copies.

I’m copying Marissa to align on contract language and Rishi for any procurement-level ask about evidence SLA. Attached: Data_Retention_Summary.pdf (one-page).

Next step: if you want contract language or a signed deletion SLA, tell me the exact acceptance criteria (what kind of proof you need) and we’ll scope it.

Best,
Kimberly Park
Director, Security & Compliance
Redwood Inference

Marissa / Rishi — forwarding HealthCo security question. Key asks we should confirm/offer:

1) Turnaround SLA for Hosted erasure evidence: customer expects a signed confirmation + audit log excerpts. Can we commit to a 7 business-day delivery for deletion evidence for hosted customers? If not, what is realistic (we normally auto-purge in 7 days but evidence packaging takes longer).

2) Attachments retention: default 90 days — is that acceptable to procurement? We can offer 30 days in contract for Dedicated.

3) Explicit language to add to SOW/DPAs: what we will delete, how we will prove deletion, and fallback if deletion impacts debugging/incident investigation (retention holds).

Suggested reply: offer the standard hosted defaults, + optional SLA add-on (for an additional fee) that guarantees deletion evidence within 10 business days, and note that Dedicated/Private deployments support custom horizons. Also attach our internal runbook for erasure (ERASURE_RUNBOOK.md) — send a redline to me if you want changes before sending to the customer.

Thoughts?
Kim

Hi Elena — following up with final language you can use in your questionnaire. I’ve included options depending on how strict you want the horizon to be.

Canonical hosted defaults (drop-in language):
- Prompts (customer-sent input): retained by default for 45 days for operational and security purposes.
- Final responses (model outputs): retained by default for 45 days; ephemeral streaming buffers are not persisted in our long-term stores.
- Streamed tokens: processed in-memory and discarded; only finalized outputs are written to storage by default.
- Customer attachments: retained up to 90 days by default; retention can be shortened via contract or via a Dedicated deployment.

Customer-initiated erasure Flow (what we commit to for Hosted customers):
- Submit erasure request via support portal or customer API endpoint.
- Internal purge job removes default-retained artifacts within 7 business days.
- Proof of deletion: Redwood will provide an evidence package consisting of (a) audit log excerpts with object identifiers and deletion timestamps, and (b) a signed deletion confirmation. Standard delivery: within 10 business days of request receipt.

Options and contractual controls:
- Add-on: Accelerated erasure evidence (deliverable within 5 business days) available as a paid SLA.
- Dedicated/Private: support for customer-configured retention horizons and direct evidence export; for on-prem, customer has the option to perform local deletion without Redwood intermediating.

If this language looks good I can provide a short paragraph for your questionnaire and attach the one-page PDF. If you need guaranteed shorter timelines or a specific certificate format, tell me the acceptance criteria (e.g., logs + SHA256 of objects removed) and we will draft an addendum.

Regards,
Kimberly Park
